outcomes: A Go and a TypeScript producer write the same bytes for the same needs
A workload's aggregated manifest merges its dependency closure by identity, with provenance, overrides and a runtime block
A deployer reads a deployment declaration in one canonical byte form and refuses any other
nonGoals: Deployer adapters that provision the declared resources
Payload schemas attached to event topics
Minimum residency and billing posture, which deployers own
The rich, secret-bearing database and storage shapes, which their own protocols own

requirements.text: A manifest carries protocolVersion 2, and the per-project and aggregated schemas accept exactly that version. Each schema definition of the per-project, aggregated and overrides shapes has the members of its Go type, no more and no fewer. The runtime subtree exposes none of the retired cost-policy fields min, billing, requestBased, cpuIdle and cpuAlwaysAllocated. Each of the six TypeScript producers of the framework stamps version 2 in its one version constant.

Every valid fixture validates and every invalid one is refused. A reader refuses an unknown member as infra.unknown_field, naming the migration for a retired cost-policy field; a runtime block in a per-project manifest as infra.runtime_in_library; bytes that are not JSON as infra.parse_error; another version, 1 included, as infra.invalid_protocol_version; and an engine but postgres, mysql, sqlite and firestore as infra.invalid_engine. The cloud infra plan prints the codes of a manifest that fails.

A resource name is lowercase and a secret name a config key, or it is infra.invalid_name. A schedule is a 5-field cron: an empty or blank one is infra.empty_schedule, and a malformed one or a macro infra.invalid_schedule. An aggregated manifest without a workload is infra.missing_workload, an entry without sources infra.missing_sources, and a contributor but manual or framework:<name>, or a source without a project, infra.invalid_contributor. A negative scaling is infra.invalid_scaling, and 0 is valid.

Merge keys a database by name and engine and unions its schemas, keeps two engines apart, and dedups topics and secrets by name. A bucket unions its access and its public flag and fills an empty retention. Two different retentions, or two schedules or entrypoints of one job, are infra.conflicting_value, which a manual contributor wins over a framework one; between equals the first source wins. Sources are sorted and deduped. The same contributions, in any order, give the same bytes.

A subscribe is a bare topic for pull delivery or an object with its topic and a stream or push delivery, so an all-pull events block keeps the bytes of a string array. The object form refuses an unknown member, and a delivery outside pull, stream and push is refused. When two projects subscribe one topic, the merged subscribe takes the strongest delivery whatever their order, and a pull one carries no delivery.

An overrides file drops from a merged manifest each entry an ignore rule names, a database by name and engine and any other entry by name, a secret by its config key, and leaves its input unchanged; an events block left empty becomes absent. A rule that matches nothing is a warning, infra.unused_override. The overrides reader refuses an unknown member, a bad engine and a bad name. The extension SDK aggregator drops a database a library declares when the workload ignores it, and keeps the rest.

DefaultRuntime returns, at each call, a fresh runtime with the default scaling max, concurrency and ingress visibility.The extension SDK aggregator gives a workload without infra/runtime.json those defaults, in its manifest and in .gen/infra/runtime.json; an authored runtime.json wins and removes that sidecar; one with scaling.min is infra.unknown_field naming the cost policy and the migration, and drops the whole runtime block. The TypeScript extension sets runtime.protocols.http2 to false in both files.

Sync folds every fragment of .gen/infra but runtime.json into infra/requirements.json, sorted and deduped, in the formatter's form: a scalar array fits one line within 120 columns, a trailing comma counted, or expands. It moves a v1 fragment to v2 with a warning, refuses an unknown member naming its fragment, and removes a stale file. A producer owns one fragment, which WriteSidecar stamps with $schema and the version and removes when empty. The TypeScript extension's generate step syncs the file.

For the inputs its golden in fixtures/equivalence documents, each producer emits that golden byte for byte: the Go database, events, migration and storage frameworks and the secrets producer of the Go extension, and the TypeScript database, events, migration, document, storage and runtime config producers. A Go and a TypeScript producer of one kind therefore write the same bytes.

MarshalDeployment writes a manifest that validates as compact bytes in member order, without $schema or a final newline, the same at each call, and nothing for one that does not. ParseDeployment refuses indented, reordered, newline-ended, repeated-member, $schema or unescaped bytes as infra.non_canonical. The extension SDK and the TypeScript extension declare the build aggregate in those bytes. The cloud publish stores them as they are and refuses a missing, non-canonical or other workload's declaration.

The database entries are the engine-mapped image of the database protocol's projection, sorted by name, and the storage entries the access-mapped image of the storage protocol's; an unmapped engine is infra.invalid_engine and an unmapped access infra.invalid_access, each dropping its entry, and none invents a schema or an access. The encoded database entries carry no connection, DSN, host, user, password or SSL member, and the storage entries no backend, bucket, prefix, identity, scope or signer.
